2026-10-19.text: Quiet Monday, and Squamish is the only spot with real odds: SW 12 to 13 from 1pm to 4pm, about 50 to 60% for 12kt. I’m not sold yet. Pam Rocks is still blowing an outflow at N 14 at 8am, the valley is 5°C colder than Pam Rocks, and Pemberton’s pressure is 2 hPa above Vancouver’s. That’s the same setup as yesterday, when the page had 9 for the afternoon and the Spit only did 3. Before driving up, I want Pam Rocks under 8kt and turning south by noon, and Squamish at least 2°C warmer than Pam Rocks by 1pm. If that happens, think 1 to 5pm on a rising tide to 14ft at 2:23pm. If Pam Rocks is still N 10+ at noon, skip it. Everywhere else stays light, though Jericho is worth a check on the buoy after 4pm with NW 10 to 15 coming back this evening. The bigger news is tomorrow: EC has a strong wind warning for the Strait with NW 15 to 25 after midnight, and a Howe Sound outflow of 15 to 25 that could make Porteau worth a look if Pam Rocks reaches 25. Stay tuned!

2026-10-18.text:
Mostly a rest day. Howe Sound has an outflow this morning: Pam Rocks is N 19 gusting 26 at 8am. That’s short of the 25kt Porteau needs, and EC has it going light near noon, so I’m not chasing it. Squamish is a no go for me. The valley is 7°C colder than Pam Rocks, Pemberton’s pressure is still higher than Vancouver’s, and the afternoon looks cloudy, so this is the same setup as Thursday’s bust.

The one to watch is Jericho late this afternoon. The page shows WNW 8 to 9 from 4 to 7pm, and EC has NW 10 to 15 coming in early this evening. Yesterday’s afternoon westerly beat the forecast at English Bay by 5 to 8kt, so check the buoy after 3pm. If it reads 12+ from the west, go. The tide stays high all afternoon (14ft at 1:24pm), so it’s an easy launch.

2026-10-17.text:
A front came through overnight and the wind is running ahead of the forecast this morning.

The south side is the call right now. Cherry Point, across Semiahmoo Bay, went from 10 to 15 kt SW gusting 18 by 6:30am and was still building, and there are whitecaps on the White Rock cam (the sensor is down). I think White Rock and Crescent Beach are 13 to 16 kt right now, a bit more than the page shows for White Rock. Best window is about 8am to 10:30am on a rising tide, high around 1pm. It should fade late morning as the wind swings W. If Cherry Point drops under 12 or turns past 260°, it's over.

Tsawwassen is easing (Ferry Terminal 11 and Sand Heads 9 at 7am), so expect less than the page shows there.

Squamish surprised everyone: S to SE 16 to 25 kt gusting over 30 since 3am. That's not a thermal, it's the pressure behind the front pushing air up Howe Sound (Vancouver is about 5 hPa above Pemberton). The models had 8 to 9 kt and Environment Canada's S 10 to 20 was right. It's easing and gusty from the SE (16 gusting 19 at 6:50am). With the sun coming out it could pick up again from noon to 4pm.

2026-10-16.text: Outflow day. Squamish thermal unlikely (same setup as yesterday’s bust). Porteau is borderline, watch for Pam Rocks 25kt+ this morning. Everything else is light.

2026-10-15.text:
No spot on the page gets past 16% for 12kt, but Squamish is worth watching. Pam Rocks is blowing an outflow at NNW 18 gusting 23 this morning, and the forecast shows a calm afternoon. On the last few sunny October days, though, the outflow died by late morning and the thermal came in stronger and later than forecast. Yesterday was one of them: the page said 13, and the Spit did 15 to 16 from 3 to 6pm. My checks before driving up: Pam Rocks under 8kt and turning SE by noon, Squamish at least 2°C warmer than Pam Rocks by 1pm, and the Spit vane swinging south. If those line up, think 2 to 6pm. Porteau’s outflow stays short of 25kt, so I’m not chasing it.

And a big thank you to the first person who bought me my first coffee! It means a lot!

2026-10-14.text: I’m sitting Wednesday out. Squamish only gets 12 to 13kt, which isn’t worth the drive for me. I’ll watch Thursday morning’s outflow at Porteau, 15 to 25 per EC, and save my legs for Friday’s SE 15 to 25.

2026-10-13.text: Not much going on today. Squamish might get some inflow this afternoon, but it looks weak: the temperature difference isn’t really there, and the cloud cover should knock it down further. Forecast has it peaking around 11 to 12 knots at 2 to 3pm, so marginal at best. Will keep an eye on the rest of the week!

2026-10-12.text: Light day: Squamish is the only call, with a SW thermal at 15kt gusting 19 from 2pm to 5pm. It has about 80% odds of 12kt, but under 20% for 18kt, with small chop and no tide limit. Everywhere else is under 8kt. We missed the outflow at Porteau yesterday: Pam Rocks hit 25 to 30 and riders scored great swell, but the site showed only 7 to 14kt. The fix went live yesterday afternoon and we’ll check it on the next outflow. Next up: Howe Sound inflow 10 to 20 on Tuesday, SE 20 to 25 on Wednesday morning.

2026-10-11.text:
Another light one for most of us, with one surprise this morning. Howe Sound is blowing a proper outflow: Pam Rocks read NNE 25 gusting 32 at 8am, which is strong enough for Porteau to work. If you're close and quick, that's the strongest wind of the day, and the tide is dropping until about 12:40pm so the swell should hold. Environment Canada has it fading to 5 to 15 near noon, so don't wait.

For everyone else, Jericho is my pick again from 2pm to 5pm, about 14 to 15 kt W gusting 17, with small waves building to 2 ft later in the afternoon. The launch gets easier after 3pm when the tide is back over 10 ft. Environment Canada is calling NW 15 to 20 late this afternoon, a bit more than the models, so watch the live readings.

Squamish is the wildcard. The models keep it on a northerly outflow until mid afternoon, then a light southerly under 10 kt. They said the same yesterday and the Spit ran 15 to 20 on inflow from 1pm to 4pm. Today's outflow is much stronger, so I wouldn't count on a repeat, but it's full sun again. If Pam Rocks swings south by noon, it may be worth the drive. Bring the big wing!

2026-10-10.text: I hope everyone is tired from yesterday, but if you didn’t get enough... here is what’s on the menu for today. It’s a lighter one. The NW comes back this afternoon and Jericho is my pick from 2pm to 6pm, about 14 to 16 kt W to WNW, with an easier launch after 3pm when the tide is back over 10 ft. Environment Canada is calling NW 15 to 20 from noon, which is more and earlier than the models show, so keep an eye on the live readings around lunch. Squamish has a gusty northerly outflow of 12 to 15 kt gusting 23, and it only gets strong after dark. Bring the big wing!

2026-10-09.text: The NW system is here and today is the day. I believe Steveston is the pick, with 22 to 24 kt WNW gusting 30 from 8am to 5pm and good swell of 3 to 4 ft, plus a possible epic window before 10am while the tide is still falling against the wind. Jericho will be on all day too, but it looks very strong midday, with 30 kt plus and gusts near 40 from 10am to 3pm, swell up to 6 ft, and a long walk at low tide from about 9am to 2pm, so early morning or after 3pm is the easier call there. Crescent Beach has a short window until about 9am with 22 to 25 kt before the wind turns too far NW. Squamish looks lighter at around 17 kt in the afternoon, and I would skip the rest. Environment Canada has a strong wind warning with NW 20 to 30 this morning, easing to 15 to 20 by evening. Salmon are running in the Fraser, so watch your foil at Steveston. Have fun out there!
